in_text_mentions: lic head with sparse wispy hair, a small nose with hypoplastic alae, a prominent columella, small-appearing palpebral fissures, a small cornea, microphthalmia, a wide anterior fontanelle, and retrognathia (Figure 1). Syndactyly of digits 4 and 5 and webbing of digits 3 and 4 of the right (Figure 2) and left hands were present. Cardiac echocardiogram on the day of birth showed the presence of a mild patent ductus arteriosus, mild patent foramen ovale, and a normal aorta. Feeding difficulties were exacerbated by the presence of the omphalocele; surgical correction was performed on day 2 of life.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (1, 2, 3, 4). 1: Top-left facial photo of same ODDD patient; shows pinched nasal morphology and abnormal dentition corresponding to enamel defect described in text. 2: Bilateral hand photo shows finger anomalies matching in-text hand, finger anomaly with partial syndactyly and clinodactyly in ODDD article. 3: Bilateral foot photo shows toe anomaly with hypoplasia and wide distance between toes and thumbs as described in text for this ODDD patient; no foot-specific term in vocabulary so captured as proposed. 4: Close-up perioral photo shows abnormal dentition corresponding to enamel defect in ODDD patient.

Digital and dental malformation and short stature in a patient with neurological problems: a variant of the oculodentodigital dysplasia syndrome or a new syndrome?. Iranian journal of child neurology 2012. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure s(1-4).
panels.figure_caption: Physical characteristic features of the patient
in_text_mentions: enamel. She had hand, finger and toe anomaly (hypoplasia of the distal and middle phalanges and partial syndactyly of the first, second and third fingers, clinodactyly, wide distance between the fingers, toes and thumbs and hypoplasia. Cubitus valgus was another limb abnormality that was seen on examination (Figures 1-4). She had spastic and ataxic gait (spasticity especially in the lower limbs). Tremor, hyperreflexia and clonus were seen on examination. Cerebellar examination such as the finger to nose and heel to sheen tests was disrupted. She had immature behavior, but normal intelligence.
